newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Iraq's return well-absorbed by market - Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's return well-absorbed by market - Venezuela.

text.p: The amount of Iraqi oil allowed back on the markets has been well absorbed, which shows that some analysts had underestimated demand, Venezuelan Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta said Monday.
"The market is absorbing perfectly well Iraq's return, thanks of course to an increase in demand for seasonal reasons," he told reporters.
Arrieta noted that the average export price of Venezuela's oil basket was $21.21 in December and $18.17 this year, up from $14.84 in 1995, and "it had fallen under $20 when Iraq returned."
He also said that "obviously the level of stocks is not as high as last year".

The United Nations, under an oil-for-food agreement with Iraq that went into effect on December 10, allowed Baghdad to sell up to $2 billion worth of oil over six months in order to buy humanitarian goods.
